anomalies.observed: C5 is labelled "1000uF 10v solid" and sits on the VMOT motor-power rail, which the drawing also feeds to motor MOSFET circuits (Q2-Q4) and to other 47uF/63V and 100V capacitors (C1, C28, C34) on the same rail.
anomalies.expected: A bulk capacitor on a motor supply that is elsewhere rated 63V or 100V should carry a voltage rating with margin over the rail voltage. A 10V rating on VMOT would be marginal or unsafe if the motor supply runs at 12V or higher.

evidence.quote: C5 1000uF 10v solid (Power sheet, near VMOT, GND)
C1 47uF 63V solid; C28 47uF 63V solid; C34 4.7uF 100V (VMOT area)
notes.txt (motherboard section): "Fix the footprint/pad size for C5 - 8mm diameter too small."

anomalies.impact: If VMOT is above 10V, the bulk capacitor could be overstressed, leading to failure, venting or loss of bulk decoupling on the motor power rail. The spec's known C5 footprint issue does not cover the voltage rating, so this may be a real rating error.

anomalies.observed: The same R48 pull-up on the gate of Q9 (AO3401A) is printed as "10K" in one tile and as "210K" in another tile of the same sheet.
anomalies.expected: The gate pull-up of a P-channel MOSFET switch is normally 10K, as on the matching Q6 stage (R58 10K). A 210K value would give a much weaker pull-up and a slower or less reliable turn-off.

evidence.quote: Q9 AO3401A 1 3 R48 210K (same sheet, second tile)

anomalies.impact: The conflicting values make the gate drive for Q9 uncertain. If the 210K value is the built value, the switch may turn off slowly or not fully, which would change the power-sequencing behaviour.

parsed.summary: The drawing is dense and most passives match their roles, but two values look suspicious: the 10V bulk capacitor C5 on the VMOT motor rail and conflicting 10K/210K values for the Q9 gate pull-up R48. Both are low-confidence and cannot be confirmed from the image alone.
